name: Blindsee Biberwier
kurzbeschreibung: Blindsee lake near Biberwier at 1,093 m on the Fernpass: turquoise-blue high mountain lake with a sunken forest, a diving Eldorado, and Zugspitze views.
beschreibung:
Overview

The breathtaking Blindsee lake near Biberwier is undoubtedly one of the most spectacular high mountain lakes in the entire Tyrolean Zugspitz Arena. Situated at an alpine altitude of exactly 1,093 meters directly below the historic Fernpass in a pristine high mountain basin, the deep blue to turquoise waters impress with their sensational visibility depth and the monumental alpine backdrop of the rugged Mieminger Chain. This fascinating mountain lake was formed millennia ago by a massive prehistoric rockslide from the surrounding peaks, whose huge boulders still characterize the shore today. Due to its rich fish population and the bizarre, sunken tree trunks on the bottom, Blindsee is also an internationally highly valued paradise for scuba divers.

Route & Requirements

The classic circumnavigation of the mountain lake via the marked lakeside hiking trail is a moderately difficult alpine hike with a pure walking time of about two and a half hours over approximately 5.5 kilometers. While the northern section runs along wider, shady forest paths, the natural southern trail requires reliable sure-footedness: narrow forest paths wind here over scree slopes, washed-out rock ledges, and tangled roots directly above the steep bank. Hikers should have a solid basic fitness level and ankle-high hiking boots with a non-slip profile sole, as damp rock sections, fallen autumn leaves, and wet gravel sections require special alpine attention with every step.

Visit & Arrival

The lake is freely accessible during the snow-free months from May to October, with swimming in the refreshing mountain water permitted at your own risk. Scuba diving requires prior permission or a day pass from the nearby Hotel Mohr Life Resort. Arrival by car is via the Fernpass road B179; below the pass summit, a paved, toll-required access road with an automatic barrier leads directly down to the large lake parking lot. Alternatively, you can hike from the center of Biberwier via historic Roman paths on a very varied scenic hike of about one and a half hours up to the glittering lakeshore.

Tips

Don't forget your camera: from the well-known rest stop on the Fernpass federal road, there is a world-famous photo view of the luminous Blindsee with the majestic Zugspitze in the background. An early morning visit rewards hikers with absolutely calm, mirror-smooth water, in which the surrounding limestone massifs are photogenically reflected. Since there are no refreshment facilities directly on the natural lakeshore, it is advisable to bring enough drinking water and a hearty Tyrolean snack in your hiking backpack to enjoy the magnificent mountain panorama in peace.
preis: Lake freely accessible; toll road to the lakeshore approx. €8.00 per car
oeffnungszeiten: May to Oct/Nov freely accessible (snow-covered/restricted in winter)
